decided: Project sensors are declared in the project's settings as a list of separate words, never as one command line, and orbit runs one only after the user has approved that exact set on this machine. Orbit keeps a fingerprint of the approved set, and of any project file the commands name, in the user's own settings. Any change to them stops them running until the user approves again, and meanwhile each counts as firing. Orbit also records when each approval was given.
alternatives: declare them only in the user's own per-machine settings, never in the project
have the AI session run them instead of orbit
why: A cloned project must not be able to run programs on someone's machine just because they use orbit in it, and the AI being watched must not be able to quietly change what watches it; requiring approval again after any change does both, while still letting sensors travel with the project.

defines.definition: A check orbit runs over the code, the change and its history that reports whether a run has gone off course.
A sensor a project adds itself, by naming a command (such as a linter) whose output orbit reads.
